challenges.name: ship-a-breaking-change-safely-evidence
challenges.title: Ship a Breaking Change Safely: read the evidence
challenges.description: Since API release 2026.10.22-2 the Android app 3.8 crashes on every catalog screen. Six statements on one evidence pack - the release notes (A), the mapper diff (B), the crash reports (C), the API log by app version (D) and the OpenAPI diff (E) - take you from reading the evidence to a hypothesis, past two wrong explanations, to the fix and how to verify it.

questions.question:
Evidence C - crash reports, CodeDev Android, since Thu 22 Oct 16:44:
Fatal Exception: kotlinx.serialization.MissingFieldException
Fields [rating, instructor] are required for type with serial name 'dev.codedev.api.CourseDto', but they were missing at path: $.items[0]
  at dev.codedev.catalog.CatalogRepository.load(CatalogRepository.kt:58)
App 3.8.2 (382): 1,912 crashes, 1,340 users    App 3.9.0 (390): 0 crashes
App 3.8 model: data class CourseDto(val id: String, val slug: String, val title: String, val rating: Double?, val ratingCount: Int, val instructor: InstructorDto, val price: Long), decoded with Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }
Android 3.8 is 40% of Android users; the minimum-version gate cannot force an update for two weeks.

Evidence D - API gateway log, GET /v1/courses*, Thu 22 Oct 16:40-17:20, grouped by X-App-Version:
client              requests   2xx      same device again within 60 s
web 2026.10.22-2      48,210   99.98%    3%
android 3.9.0         21,804   99.97%    4%
android 3.8.2         14,390   99.98%   71%

Statement: "The API answered Android 3.8 with 2xx like every other client; the app crashes afterwards, while decoding the response body."
questions.explanation: True. D shows 99.98% 2xx for android 3.8.2, the same as for the web app and 3.9, so the server did not fail the requests. C shows where the failure happens: kotlinx.serialization throws MissingFieldException while turning the JSON into CourseDto, in CatalogRepository.load. The 71% "same device again within 60 s" for 3.8 is the crash-and-relaunch pattern, not retries after server errors. The common mistake is to trust a green API dashboard: a breaking contract change shows up as client crashes, not as 5xx on the server.

questions.question:
Evidence B - mapper diff (src/courses/course.mapper.ts):
 export function toCourseDto(row: CourseRow): CourseDto {
   return {
     id: row.id,
     slug: row.slug,
     title: row.title,
-    rating: row.ratingAvg,
+    averageRating: row.ratingAvg,
     ratingCount: row.ratingCount,
-    instructor: { id: row.instructorId, name: row.instructorName },
+    teacher: { id: row.instructorId, name: row.instructorName },
-    price: row.priceVnd,
+    price: String(row.priceVnd),
   };
 }

Evidence C - crash reports, CodeDev Android, since Thu 22 Oct 16:44:
Fatal Exception: kotlinx.serialization.MissingFieldException
Fields [rating, instructor] are required for type with serial name 'dev.codedev.api.CourseDto', but they were missing at path: $.items[0]
  at dev.codedev.catalog.CatalogRepository.load(CatalogRepository.kt:58)
App 3.8.2 (382): 1,912 crashes, 1,340 users    App 3.9.0 (390): 0 crashes
App 3.8 model: data class CourseDto(val id: String, val slug: String, val title: String, val rating: Double?, val ratingCount: Int, val instructor: InstructorDto, val price: Long), decoded with Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }
Android 3.8 is 40% of Android users; the minimum-version gate cannot force an update for two weeks.

Evidence E - OpenAPI diff, CI job "api-contract" (allow_failure: true) on release/2026.10.22-2:
GET /v1/courses 200  items[].rating         required property removed   BREAKING
GET /v1/courses 200  items[].instructor     required property removed   BREAKING
GET /v1/courses 200  items[].price          type integer -> string      BREAKING
GET /v1/courses 200  items[].averageRating  property added              safe
GET /v1/courses 200  items[].teacher        property added              safe
(the same 5 changes on GET /v1/courses/{slug})
Job result: 3 breaking changes - marked as warning, pipeline continued.

Statement: "The crash is caused by the rating rename alone: putting `rating` back into the response would stop the 3.8 crashes."
questions.explanation: False. The exception in C lists two missing fields, rating and instructor, and B shows both were renamed. Restoring rating alone leaves instructor missing, and 3.8 keeps crashing on the same line. E shows a third breaking change, price from integer to string, which 3.8 declares as Long; whether one decoder happens to tolerate a quoted number is not something to bet a release on. The misconception is to fix the field named in the release notes instead of every change that the diff and the contract report show.

Statement: "Android 3.8 has a JSON parsing bug: a correct client treats missing fields as null, so the fix belongs in the app, not in the API."
questions.explanation: False. The published contract before the release (the base of the diff in E) listed rating and instructor as required properties, and 3.8 decodes exactly that: rating may be null but its key must be present, instructor must be an object. The client was correct for the contract it was built against; the API broke the contract. Even an app fix would not reach the 3.8 builds already installed. The misconception is that clients should defend against any change: a contract exists so they do not have to, and the side that changes it is responsible for staying compatible.

questions.question:
Evidence A - release notes, CodeDev API 2026.10.22-2 (Thu 22 Oct, 16:40):
- Course DTO cleanup: renamed `rating` to `averageRating` and `instructor` to `teacher`; `price` is now a decimal string.
- Web app 2026.10.22-2, deployed together with the API, reads the new fields.
- Android 3.9.0 (released 15 Oct) already accepts both the old and the new names.

Evidence C - crash reports, CodeDev Android, since Thu 22 Oct 16:44:
Fatal Exception: kotlinx.serialization.MissingFieldException
Fields [rating, instructor] are required for type with serial name 'dev.codedev.api.CourseDto', but they were missing at path: $.items[0]
  at dev.codedev.catalog.CatalogRepository.load(CatalogRepository.kt:58)
App 3.8.2 (382): 1,912 crashes, 1,340 users    App 3.9.0 (390): 0 crashes
App 3.8 model: data class CourseDto(val id: String, val slug: String, val title: String, val rating: Double?, val ratingCount: Int, val instructor: InstructorDto, val price: Long), decoded with Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }
Android 3.8 is 40% of Android users; the minimum-version gate cannot force an update for two weeks.

Statement: "Publishing an Android 3.10 build today leaves the 3.8 users crashing until each of them updates, which the team cannot force for two weeks, so the API has to keep serving what 3.8 reads."
questions.explanation: True. A new app version only helps the users who install it. C says 3.8 is 40% of Android users and the minimum-version gate cannot force them off it for two weeks, so "roll forward the app" leaves them crashing for up to two weeks. Mobile apps are the clearest case of clients you do not deploy: old versions stay installed for months. The misconception is to treat a mobile client like the web app, which is replaced on the next page load; the fix has to be on the server.

Evidence A - release notes, CodeDev API 2026.10.22-2 (Thu 22 Oct, 16:40):
- Course DTO cleanup: renamed `rating` to `averageRating` and `instructor` to `teacher`; `price` is now a decimal string.
- Web app 2026.10.22-2, deployed together with the API, reads the new fields.
- Android 3.9.0 (released 15 Oct) already accepts both the old and the new names.

Evidence B - mapper diff (src/courses/course.mapper.ts):
 export function toCourseDto(row: CourseRow): CourseDto {
   return {
     id: row.id,
     slug: row.slug,
     title: row.title,
-    rating: row.ratingAvg,
+    averageRating: row.ratingAvg,
     ratingCount: row.ratingCount,
-    instructor: { id: row.instructorId, name: row.instructorName },
+    teacher: { id: row.instructorId, name: row.instructorName },
-    price: row.priceVnd,
+    price: String(row.priceVnd),
   };
 }

Statement: "The safest fix is to undo the rename in the API only: ship the mapper exactly as it was before 22 Oct (rating, instructor, integer price) and leave the web app as it is."
questions.explanation: False. A says web app 2026.10.22-2 now reads averageRating, teacher and the string price, so reverting only the API fixes 3.8 and breaks the web app, the largest client in D. The fix that keeps every client working is expand/contract: serve the old fields with their old types next to the new ones (the string price under a new name, priceAmount, because one field cannot have two types), mark the old ones deprecated with Deprecation and Sunset headers, and remove them only after the sunset date, once the logs show the 3.8 traffic is gone. The misconception is that undoing a change is always safe: other clients may already depend on the new shape.

Statement: "A contract test that checks real API responses against two schemas - what Android 3.8 decodes (rating key present, instructor an object, price an integer) and what the web app decodes - would have failed on release 2026.10.22-2 and passes after the expand fix."
questions.explanation: True. On 2026.10.22-2 the old-client schema fails on every course (rating and instructor missing, price a string), so the test fails before the deploy. After the expand fix both schemas pass, because each response carries the old and the new fields. Validating real responses also catches what the OpenAPI diff in E cannot: a mapper that disagrees with the document. The test has to stay until the contract step, so nobody removes rating early. The misconception is to verify a compatibility fix by opening the app once on a test phone: one device checks one version, the schemas check every response.

challenges.name: ship-a-breaking-change-safely
challenges.title: Ship a Breaking Change Safely
challenges.description:
Since CodeDev API release 2026.10.22-2 the Android app 3.8 (40% of Android users, cannot be force-updated for two weeks) crashes on every catalog screen with "Fields [rating, instructor] are required", while the web app, deployed together with the API, works. The release notes say "renamed rating to averageRating, cleaned up the course DTO". Fix the course mapper and add the deprecation headers so that both clients work during the migration.

Every course response must carry: the old, deprecated fields with their old types - `rating` (number or null, the key always present), `instructor` ({ id, name }) and `price` (integer, in dong); the new fields - `averageRating` (number or null, the key always present), `teacher` ({ id, name }) and `priceAmount` (the price in dong as a decimal string without separators, e.g. "149000"); and the unchanged `id`, `slug`, `title` and `ratingCount`.

`deprecationHeaders(policy)` returns the headers sent with every course response: `Deprecation` = "@" followed by `policy.deprecatedAt` in whole Unix seconds, rounded down (the RFC 9745 form, e.g. "@1792746000"); `Sunset` = `policy.sunsetAt` as an HTTP-date such as "Mon, 30 Nov 2026 00:00:00 GMT" (RFC 8594), and no `Sunset` key at all when `policy.sunsetAt` is null. It throws an Error when a date cannot be parsed, or when `sunsetAt` is earlier than 14 days after `deprecatedAt` (exactly 14 days is allowed). Dates are ISO 8601 strings with an offset.

Input (stdin, JSON): { "policy": { "deprecatedAt", "sunsetAt" }, "rows": CourseRow[] }. The test runner (do not change) checks every response against the old-client and the new-client schema and prints { responses, headers, oldClient: { failed, firstErrors }, newClient: { failed, firstErrors } }, or { "error": "invalid deprecation policy" } when deprecationHeaders throws.
hints: Which fields does app 3.8 require, and with which types? A field can only have one type in a response: where can the new string price go so that the old integer price stays?
Compare toCourseDto and the CourseDto type it returns with the old-client list in the description, field by field. Then look at what deprecationHeaders returns, and at the unit Date.parse returns.

A similar case: renaming `email` to `contactEmail` on a user response during a migration means returning both `email` and `contactEmail` with the same value. A deprecation date of 2026-01-15T00:00:00Z is 1768435200000 ms after the epoch, so its header value is "@1768435200"; a sunset of 2026-02-01T12:00:00Z is written "Sun, 01 Feb 2026 12:00:00 GMT".

tests.name: Three catalog courses, sunset on 30 Nov: both clients decode every response
No sunset date decided yet: Deprecation is sent without Sunset
A course without reviews (null rating) and a free course keep the old keys and types
Sunset exactly 14 days after deprecation is allowed; Deprecation rounds down to seconds
Sunset 13 days after deprecation is rejected (app 3.8 cannot be force-updated yet)
A sunset date that cannot be parsed is rejected
400 courses with a +07:00 deprecation date: every response passes both client checks
